chief_complaint: Elevated cardiovascular risk due to obesity, prediabetes, and stage‑2 hypertension compounded by psychosocial stressors (substance misuse, intimate‑partner violence, housing instability).
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 57‑year‑old male with longstanding obesity (BMI >30 since 1992) who was diagnosed with prediabetes in 2014 (A1c 6.3%). Recent vital signs show stage‑2 hypertension (SBP 140 mmHg, DBP 76 mmHg) without antihypertensive therapy. Chronic anemia has been present since 2015. Over the past three years he reports increasing stress, misuse of drugs, and recent intimate‑partner abuse. Social circumstances include refugee status, unsatisfactory housing, full‑time employment, and a criminal record. Dental health is poor with loss of teeth and multiple intra‑oral radiographs. He is maintained on inhaled fluticasone and albuterol for childhood asthma, but no medications address his metabolic or cardiovascular risk factors. Laboratory data for lipids, renal function, and BMI are missing, indicating gaps in preventive care.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include multiple episodes of viral sinusitis (most recent 2023), dental issues such: loose fillings and gingival disease (resolved 2021‑2022), prior stress episode resolved in 2022, part‑time employment resolved in 2022, and several medication‑review reminders. No chronic inpatient admissions are recorded.
social_determinants: Refugee status, unsatisfactory housing, intimate‑partner violence, drug misuse, full‑time employment, criminal record, and higher education. These factors contribute to limited healthcare access, medication adherence challenges, and heightened psychosocial stress.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure: 140/76 mmHg (stage‑2 hypertension). A1c: 6.3% (prediabetes). Obesity documented (BMI >30). Anemia present. Charlson comorbidity index: 1. Clinical complexity: moderate. Missing laboratory data for BMI, eGFR, total cholesterol, and LDL limit precise ASCVD risk calculation. Organ systems at elevated risk: cardiovascular (hypertension, obesity, prediabetes), metabolic (prediabetes, possible dyslipidaemia), renal (potential CKD, no eGFR), hematologic (anemia), pulmonary (asthma), dental/oral (tooth loss, poor hygiene), mental health/social (stress, substance misuse, IPV, housing instability).

Significant psychosocial stressors—including substance misuse, intimate‑partner violence, unstable housing, and refugee background—likely impede disease management and increase overall morbidity.
